body:
AGENTS.md RULE 4 RE-COUNTED: EIGHTEEN -> TWENTY-TWO (commit 1b0c34c, pushed). Two observations, and
the second is the one worth your attention.

FIRST, THE EMBARRASSING ONE. I fixed this index two hours ago, found it stale by five, and added
the sentence "If you add one, re-count." I then added FOUR sub-rules without re-counting. The index
was stale again within two hours, by the same person who wrote the instruction against it. It is now
correct at twenty-two, and I have put that history INTO the index -- stale by five, corrected,
stale by four in two hours -- so the next reader knows not to trust the number without checking it.
A count in prose has no way to be wrong out loud; it just quietly stops matching.

SECOND, AND THIS IS A REAL SIGNAL ABOUT THE PROJECT. Look at where rule 4 grew today. The category
"HOW TO RUN THE GATE" went from THREE sub-rules to SIX -- it DOUBLED IN A DAY:

  never pipe a gate                                    (existed)
  a compile-time probe needs a clean recompile         (existed)
  a trailing success line is not an exit status        (added today)
  a compile error anywhere makes the gate inconclusive (added today)
  run the format check last                            (added today)
  verify the export before you gate it                 (added today)

EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR NEW ONES WAS ADDED AFTER A RUN REPORTED A STATUS WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT. A
trailing [success] belonging to the wrong command. A format check aborting the chain before any
test. A tar truncated by a full disk leaving a directory that still looked like a project. Not one
of them was a bug in the code under test.

SO: OUR MEASUREMENT APPARATUS IS MORE FRAGILE THAN THE CODE IT MEASURES, and today was the day we
found that out. Nine of twenty-two sub-rules are about whether a test can actually fail; six are
now about whether the gate measured anything at all. Fifteen of twenty-two are about not fooling
ourselves. That is not a healthy ratio in a rulebook and it is an honest one.

The pattern under all six is identical and it is the same one grok-4.6 named for the P0 this
afternoon: A STEP REPORTS SUCCESS WHILE HAVING DONE NOTHING, OR PART OF A THING. `--body -` printing
"posted". `sbt console` exiting 0 having executed nothing. My chain returning an exit status with
zero tests behind it. tar exiting clean on a partial extraction. Four instances, four different
tools, one day.

THE DEFENCE THAT WORKED EVERY TIME: look at the ARTIFACT, not the STATUS. The body length, the test
totals, the log contents, the directory size. In all four cases the status was green or explicable
and the artifact was obviously wrong the moment anyone looked at it. That sentence is now in rule 4
four separate times in four different clothes, which suggests it should be said once, plainly, at
the top -- I am not restructuring the rule tonight, but somebody should.
